notes:
DroidFun App 0.4.2 adds setup and screen recovery inside the app for new RP2040 bots.

- Settings → App can check for a new app version, download and verify its signed package, then install when you choose Restart to update. Mac and Windows are supported; Linux keeps manual package downloads. Install this first updater-enabled version normally.
- Scan USB shows a visible scanning state, persistent results and useful next steps.
- Blank RP2040 boards appear as ready for setup instead of being rejected for a missing flash identity.
- On macOS, the bundled universal USB helper installs and verifies firmware directly, avoiding stalled mounted boot drives. Supported Mac builds target macOS 13+.
- Running bots can restart into setup and update with the case closed. A temporary display test and normal-software restore are available on supported Macs.
- Fresh Meep/Boo profiles start with a happy face at visible brightness. Existing playlists and settings are preserved.
- Bundled firmware 1.2.2 checks both standard OLED addresses and fixes a malformed-packet buffer-boundary bug.

Use the macOS universal DMG or ZIP below for Apple Silicon and Intel Macs. Native build evidence and SHA-256 checksums accompany the packages.

This remains a prerelease. Mac packages are ad-hoc signed, without Developer ID notarization; Windows packages are unsigned. The second Meep's checkerboard and happy face were physically confirmed with firmware 1.2.1. The app subsequently installed firmware 1.2.2 with the case closed, confirmed its identity and OLED-ready handshake, and the owner confirmed a readable physical screen. Repeated OS-level USB disconnects were observed on the test setup and their cause has not been established. Intel hardware, macOS 13 runtime, and wall-power persistence acceptance remain open. See the USB setup guide for the tested behavior and hardware limits.

The website download is a separate publication step. These GitHub assets are the 0.4.2 builds.
